pr_title: Add JsonObject ordering and extension data support
pr_body:
As a follow-up to https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/51025 add the features:
- Ability to have `JsonObject` extension properties via:
`[JsonExtensionData] public JsonObject ExtensionData {get; set;}`
  - Done in a linker-friendly way so the source-gen effort will be able to trim `JsonNode` out.
  - Today only `(I)Dictionary<string, JsonElement>` is supported as an extension property. Since `JsonElement` is read-only, it can't be effectively used for modifying extension data, so supporting `JsonObject` will enable that scenario.
- Deterministic ordering semantics so subsequent Remove() and Add() do not change the ordering of existing items. New items are appended. It is possible now to add methods like "AddBefore(node)" and "AddAfter(node)" if desired.
  - Internally the items are held by a `List<>` but once a threshold is hit an additional `Dictionary<>` is created for fast lookup by property name. Once the dictionary is created, both are kept in sync. Enumeration is always done by the list for deterministic ordering.

Minor items:
- Converter refactoring of the `System.Object` converter to detect whether to use `JsonElement` or JsonNode. Previously, the `JsonNode` converter handled this and the `System.Object` converter only knew about `JsonElement`. That could cause issues for users that ask for the converter for `System.Object`.
- Additional test coverage.
- Misc feedback from original PR.

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/51572
(no longer using an `IDictionary` field; instead `Dictionary<>` used).

issue_context.title: [Blazor WASM] - Investigate 6% size regression in System.Collections.dll.br
issue_context.body:
Size increase in System.Collections.dll.br as observed in https://msit.powerbi.com/groups/me/apps/54e0e83f-07bc-45bf-87b7-a7677ff3af2a/dashboards/fa051820-ff60-4d40-8a08-bdcc1b47b1d0


![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/46026722/115444696-ea44f280-a1e2-11eb-97b5-5455b7a02396.png)


cc @CoffeeFlux - is this worth investigating ?
comments: I couldn't figure out the best area label to add to this issue. If you have write-permissions please help me learn by adding exactly one [area label](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/docs/area-owners.md).

Likely related to https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/51571. Seeing lots of infrastructure to support `SortedDictionary` and `SortedSet` coming back into the assembly. Will track down the callers.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1746272/115482487-a9a9a100-a203-11eb-86ce-85cb47bee1aa.png)

I believe the code path below is responsible for this regression.

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/ccc25a90082fa6592eeca8e146ff37e1b7d6b79d/src/libraries/System.Text.Json/src/System/Text/Json/Node/JsonObject.IDictionary.cs#L108-L124

In particular, on line 120, there's a call to `Dictionary.Remove(string)`. However, the `Dictionary` property getter is typed as `IDictionary<,>`, backed by an `IDictionary<,>` field. This means that the linker needs to keep every possible implementation of `IDictionary<,>.Remove` around, and in the case of `SortedDictionary<,>` that means also keeping much of the `SortedSet<>` infrastructure around as well.

If the `Dictionary` property getter is changed to be a strongly-typed `Dictionary<,>` rather than an interface `IDictionary<,>` I believe this might resolve the issue, since the target method will now be statically known rather than a virtual dispatch.

cc @steveharter. This overlaps with the effort to use a strongly-typed sorted dictionary to store `JsonObject` values (to preserve insertion order when enumerating over the object).

---

That aside, this is related to https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/51311 and my comment here https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/51571#issuecomment-824145051.

review_comments: Is this because the serializer handles `null`?
Yes. At one point in the prototyping this was necessary; test code coverage confirmed it wasn't necessary.
Can revert this diff after https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/51897 is merged.
Since `JsonNode` allows a `null` to be returned from the underlying dictionary, `null` is a valid value independent of the bool return value (whether it was found or not).
Per practice in most System.Collections types both this and `ValueCollection` could be changed into public structs.

These are for to support the IDictionary contract for
`ICollection<string> IDictionary<string, JsonNode?>.Keys` and
`ICollection<JsonNode?> IDictionary<string, JsonNode?>.Values`.

If we only used `Dictionary<>` as the internal implementation then we would just delegate to the dictionary's implementation of these methods instead of adding these `KeyCollection` and `ValueCollection` classes. However, since we use a list until the threshold is hit, these extra types are just used for that and thus are hidden.
Should we add tests to guard against custom user types with the same full name?
Do we do this elsewhere to your knowledge? Note I added an assembly check to prevent this.

We wanted to add such tests for immutable collection (de)serialization since it is based on strings and reflection, but ran into issues because we couldn't force custom types to have the right assembly name (since the test assembly is `System.Text.Json.Tests`). Okay to ignore since the intent is almost certainly malicious if the type has the same assembly name.
